input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The guard uses all(...) instead of any(...) over the arguments' help attributes, so the section is gated on every argument being documented rather than on at least one.
- failure path: A command with arguments SRC (help set) and DST (no help) prints no 'Positional arguments' section at all in --help, silently dropping the documented text; conversely a command with zero arguments satisfies all([]) and prints an empty 'Positional arguments' header on every --help.

Reviewer finding
- description: The fallback '(arg.make_metavar(ctx), "")' runs even for arguments whose get_help_record returned None because they are hidden, so hidden arguments now appear in help output.
- rationale: Trigger: an Argument with hidden=True and help set. get_help_record returns None for hidden params, and the fallback then adds its metavar as a visible row. The user sees an argument the author chose to hide, which changes help output for hidden parameters.
critique: The finding is about a fallback that adds rows for hidden arguments, which leaks those arguments into help output. The labeled defect is the all()-vs-any() guard that suppresses the section when only some arguments have help, and prints an empty header when there are no arguments. These are different mechanisms.
